explanation: The E138K mutation, located ~43 Å from etravirine in the palm domain, most likely confers resistance through an indirect allosteric mechanism rather than direct contact disruption. The charge reversal from acidic glutamate to basic lysine, combined with a substantial volume increase, likely distorts the precise geometry of the NNRTI-binding pocket by altering the conformational landscape of the palm subdomain—either destabilizing the ligand-bound conformation or shifting the equilibrium toward a non-productive state that accommodates etravirine less favorably. Given the negligible ΔΔG effect (-0.006 kcal/mol), this mutation causes only marginal resistance, suggesting the allosteric perturbation is modest and etravirine retention remains largely intact despite the distant structural rearrangement.
